chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, regarding this verse:
'Nay, it is clear signs in the chests of those who have been given knowledge'
Then he said: 'By Allah, O Abu Muhammad! It does not mean what is between the two covers of the Mushaf.'
I said, 'Who are they, may I be sacrificed for you?' He said: 'Who could they possibly be other than us?'

key_terms.آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ: Clear signs/manifest verses — the divine knowledge preserved in the Imams' chests
key_terms.الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ: Those granted knowledge — the Imams according to Shia interpretation
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you — honorific formula used when addressing the Imam
key_terms.دَفَّتَيِ الْمُصْحَفِ: The two covers of the Mushaf — referring to the physical Quran codex
key_terms.صُدُورِ: Chests — metaphor for the heart/mind as the seat of preserved knowledge

ai.seo_question: Who are 'those given knowledge' in Quran 29:49 according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) interprets Quran 29:49 — 'clear signs in the chests of those given knowledge' — as referring exclusively to the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt, not to the written Quran codex. This hadith was transmitted through Abu Basir, a trusted companion of the Imam, and reflects the Shia theological doctrine that divine knowledge is entrusted to and preserved by the Imams. The rhetorical question 'Who could they possibly be other than us?' underscores the exclusivity of this knowledge to the Ahl al-Bayt.
